THIS CIVIL REVISION PETITION HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD  ON 11.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE  FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:205 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025  3
The challenge in this Civil Revision Petition is to the orders dated 10.01.2020 in I.A. No. 8201 of 2019 and O.P.(PMP) No.234 of 2018 on the file of the Additional District Court - II, Ernakulam.
The Revision Petitioner is the owner in possession of 24.64 Ares of property in Re.Sy.No.414 in Block No.6 of Thrikkakara North Village.

On 03.09.2010, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (Government of India) published notification No.S.O.2170 (E) acquiring the right of user of 8.16 Ares of property for the purpose of laying pipeline for transportation of natural gas.

sentences.text: 4. The District Court dismissed the Original Petition as barred by limitation.
5. This order is under challenge in this Civil Revision Petition.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.1 and the learned Government Pleader.
7. The Original Petition was filed by the petitioner on 24.10.2018.
The petitioner received information regarding the award on 24.04.2013, the date on which she received the compensation.
While filing the Original Petition seeking enhanced compensation, the petitioner had not filed an application for condoning the delay in filing the petition.
2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 8.

As per the Rules, any party aggrieved by the determination of the amount of compensation may prefer the application seeking enhanced compensation to the District Judge not later than 90 days of the receipt of the intimation from the competent authority under Rule 4(3).
As the petitioner did not file any application seeking condonation of delay, the District Judged dismissed the Original Petition.

9. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that after passing of the award by the competent authority, the Government considered the inadequacy of the compensation and passed several orders restructuring the method of fixing fair value and market value.
The learned counsel submitted that the latest order in that series was passed on 01.12.2017 by the Government.

It is submitted that the petitioner was of the bona fide belief that the limitation period for filing an application seeking enhanced compensation, as provided in Rule 5, commenced with the final decision following the latest Government order.
It is submitted that this was the reason why the petitioner did 2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 not file an application seeking condonation of delay.
The learned counsel now conceded that the limitation for filing the application seeking enhanced compensation started on 25.04.2013.
It is further submitted that the petitioner could establish sufficient explanation for the delay caused in making the application.
The petitioner, therefore, filed CMA seeking condonation of delay and prayed for considering the same on merits.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the respondents resisted the application and submitted that the petitioner failed to establish any convincing reason for condoning the delay of 1917 days.
The learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner had knowledge regarding the passing of the compensation by the competent authority as early as in 2013.
11. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-

Even during the process of acquiring the right of user, the petitioner pointed out mistakes in the preparation of the valuation statement, but respondent No.2 did not consider 2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 them.
Meanwhile, the Government issued G.O.(Rt)No. 3195/13/RD dated 04.06.2013 increasing the compensation by fixing the market value of the acquired land as 5 times the fair value.
The petitioner was of the impression that respondent No.2 will re-fix the compensation based on the 2013 Government Order.
The general public conducted several protests resisting the process of acquisition during different stages.
The Government considered the inadequacy of the compensation and passed revised orders restructuring the method of fixing fair value and market value.

On 01.12.2017,
the Government issued G.O. (Rt)No.5165/2017/RD fixing the compensation as 10 times the notified fair value of the land.
The petitioner submitted a representation dated 16.12.2017 to respondent No.1 for getting additional compensation based on G.O. dated 01.12.2017.
However, the competent authority did not respond to the representation.

It was at that point of time that the petitioner filed the Original Petition on the bonafide belief that the limitation starts from the date on which the competent authority is expected to take decision based on 2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 the G.O. dated 01.12.2017.
12.
The learned counsel appearing for the respondents resisted the contentions of the petitioner.
It is submitted that G.O. dated 01.12.2017 has no relevance to the fixation of compensation by the competent authority.
13. This Court is now concerned with the question whether the petitioner could establish sufficient cause for condoning the delay of 1917 days in preferring the Original Petition.
As per Section 5 of the Limitation Act, if the petitioner establishes sufficient cause, depending upon the circumstances, the Court may condone the delay.
14. The expression "sufficient cause" contained in Section 5 of the Limitation Act is elastic enough to yield different results depending upon the circumstances of the case.
The criteria to be applied in condoning the delay in different claims may be different.
For example, in the case of beneficial legislations a liberal interpretation must be given to the expression "sufficient cause" to serve its object.

The concept of reasonableness demands that the 2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 courts, while taking a liberal approach, must also consider the rights and obligations of both the parties.
When a right has accrued in favour of one party due to gross negligence of the other, the Court shall refrain from exercising the discretionary relief.

It is a settled legal proposition that law of limitation may harshly affect a particular party but it has to be applied Smt. Geetha Suresh vs Gail (India)Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148869255/
4 with all its rigour when the Statute mandates so.

sentences.text: The Court has no power to extend the period of limitation on equitable grounds.
The statute of limitation is founded on public policy, its aim being to secure peace in the community, to suppress fraud and perjury, to quicken diligence and to prevent oppression.
It seeks to bury all acts of the past which have not been agitated unexplainably and have from lapse of time become stale.

(Vide: Basawaraj and Another v. Special Land Acquisition Officcer [(2013) 14 SCC 81]).
15.

sentences.text:
The expression "sufficient cause" should be given a liberal interpretation to ensure that substantial justice is done, but only so long as negligence, inaction or lack of bona fides cannot be imputed to the party 2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 concerned,
whether or not sufficient cause has been furnished, can be decided on the facts of a particular case and no straitjacket formula is possible.

(Vide: Madanlal v. Shyamlal [(2002) 1 SCC 535 : AIR 2002 SC 100], Ram Nath Sao v. Gobardhan Sao [(2002) 3 SCC 195 : AIR 2002 SC 1201]) and Basawaraj and Another v. Special Land Acquisition Officer [(2013) 14 SCC 81]).

sentences.text: 16. It is submitted that the petitioner is an illiterate lady.
Admittedly, she is seeking the rescue of a beneficial legislature.

In the present case, the petitioner was of the bonafide belief that the limitation to initiate the Original Petition would start run from the decision which should have been taken by the competent authority based on the G.O. dated 01.12.2017.
The bonafides of the petitioner are evident from the fact that she did not file any application seeking condonation of delay while filing the Original Petition.
17. In my considered view, the petitioner has established sufficient cause for condoning the delay.
2025:KER:20596 C.R.P.No.126 of 2020 and CMA No.1 of 2025 Therefore, CMA No.1/2025 is allowed.

The delay of 1917 days in filing the application to condone the delay in filing O.P.(PMP)
No.234 of 2018 stands condoned.

The order dated 10.01.2020 in I.A. No. 8201 of 2019 in O.P.(PMP)
No.234 of 2018 on the file of the Additional District Court- II, Ernakulam, stands set aside.
The Original Petition is restored to file.

It is made clear that the petitioner is not entitled to the statutory interest for the period of delay that occurred in filing the Original Petition, in the event the District Court enhances the compensation.
The Civil Revision Petition is allowed as above.
